content: The provided text is a detailed list of drug interactions involving erythromycin stearate and various other medications. 1. Oxaliplatin increases the level or effect of erythromycin stearate through mechanisms not fully understood. Use caution and monitor closely. Both oxaliplatin and erythromycin stearate prolong the QTc interval, which can lead to serious cardiac risks. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 2. Oxcarbazepine decreases the level or effect of erythromycin stearate by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzymes. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 3. Erythromycin stearate increases the level or effect of oxybutynin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Both ozanimod and erythromycin stearate prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. Avoid initiating ozanimod in patients concurrently taking QT-prolonging drugs with known arrhythmogenic properties. 5. Erythromycin stearate increases the level or effect of paclitaxel by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Erythromycin stearate increases the level or effect of paclitaxel protein-bound formulations through similar mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Erythromycin stearate increases the level or effect of pacritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 8. Erythromycin stearate increases the level or effect of palbociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Erythromycin stearate increases the level or effect of paliperidone by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, necessitating therapy modification and close monitoring. 10. Erythromycin stearate increases the level or effect of palovarotene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. Avoid coadministration with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the palovarotene dose by 50%. 11. Both erythromycin stearate and panobinostat significantly prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Panobinostat prescribing information advises against use with QT-prolonging drugs. 12. Erythromycin stearate decreases the level or effect of pantothenic acid by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral formulations of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Erythromycin stearate increases the level or effect of parecoxib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Erythromycin stearate increases the level or effect of paromomycin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Both erythromycin stearate and paroxetine prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 16. Both erythromycin stearate and pasireotide prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 17. Both erythromycin stearate and pazopanib prolong the QTc interval. Erythromycin stearate also increases the level or effect of pazopanib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the pazopanib dose to 400 mg/day. 18. Erythromycin stearate increases the level or effect of pemigatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pemigatinib dose as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, the previous pemigatinib dose may be resumed. 19. Erythromycin stearate decreases the effects of penicillin G aqueous and penicillin VK through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 20. Both erythromycin stearate and pentamidine prolong the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 21. Pentobarbital decreases the level or effect of erythromycin stearate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and increasing elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 22. Both erythromycin stearate and perphenazine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 23. Both erythromycin stearate and pexidartinib increase the risk of hepatotoxicity. Erythromycin stearate also increases the level or effect of pexidartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration with CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per the drug monograph. 24. Erythromycin stearate increases the effect of phenindione by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 25. Phenobarbital decreases the level or effect of erythromycin stearate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and increasing elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 26. Phenytoin decreases the level or effect of erythromycin stearate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 27. Both erythromycin stearate and pimozide prolong the QTc interval. Erythromycin stearate also increases pimozide levels by inhibiting its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 28. Erythromycin stearate increases the level or effect of pioglitazone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Erythromycin stearate decreases the effect of piperacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Erythromycin stearate increases the toxicity of pitavastatin by inhibiting its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Do not exceed 1 mg/day of pitavastatin. 31. Both erythromycin stearate and pitolisant prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 32. Erythromycin stearate increases the level or effect of pomalidomide by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 33. Ponatinib increases the level of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Both erythromycin stearate and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Erythromycin stearate also increases the level or effect of posaconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 35. Erythromycin stearate increases the toxicity of pravastatin by inhibiting OATP1B1 transporters, which may increase the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Erythromycin stearate increases the level or effect of prednisolone by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 37. Erythromycin stearate increases the level or effect of prednisone by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters and CYP3A4 metabolism. Prednisone also decreases the level or effect of erythromycin stearate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Pretomanid increases the level or effect of erythromycin stearate through mechanisms not fully understood. Both drugs increase each other's toxicity. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Pretomanid is associated with hepatotoxicity; avoid alcohol and other hepatotoxic agents. 39. Both erythromycin stearate and primaquine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 40. Primidone decreases the level or effect of erythromycin stearate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and increasing elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 41. Both erythromycin stearate and procainamide prolong the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 42. Both erythromycin stearate and prochlorperazine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 43. Both erythromycin stearate and promazine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 44. Both erythromycin stearate and promethazine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 45. Erythromycin stearate increases the level or effect of propafenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Erythromycin stearate increases the effect of protamine by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 47. Both erythromycin stearate and protriptyline prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 48. Erythromycin stearate decreases the level or effect of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral formulations of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Both erythromycin stearate and quetiapine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 50. Both erythromycin stearate and quinidine prolong the QTc interval. Erythromycin stearate also increases quinidine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 51. Both erythromycin stearate and quinine prolong the QTc interval. Erythromycin stearate also increases quinine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 53. Both erythromycin stearate and quizartinib prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely with frequent ECGs. 54. Erythromycin stearate increases the level or effect of rabeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 55. Erythromycin stearate increases the level or effect of ramelteon by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Both erythromycin stearate and ranolazine prolong the QTc interval. Erythromycin stearate also increases ranolazine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 57. Erythromycin stearate increases the level or effect of repaglinide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 58. Erythromycin stearate increases the level or effect of repotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 59. Erythromycin stearate increases the level or effect of resmetirom by inhibiting OATP1B1/3 transporters. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 60. Erythromycin stearate increases the level or effect of revefenacin by inhibiting OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 transporters. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 61. Ribociclib increases the level or effect of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing toxicity. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 62. Rifabutin decreases the level or effect of erythromycin stearate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
